text:
Architecture intent:
- SUSE Multi-Linux Manager remains the authoritative fleet control plane.
- Hermes runs inside an OpenShell policy sandbox and selects a fast planning model or deeper diagnostic model.
- Broad fleet operations use the Uyuni / SUSE Multi-Linux Manager MCP server.
- A direct SLES 16 MCP path is optional, narrowly permissioned, and technology preview.
- State-changing tools require ticket/approval, bounded targets, verification, and rollback.

Architecture intent:
- SUSE AI Factory with NVIDIA is shown as a management plane plus dedicated AI workload and data/fleet services.
- Rancher Prime, RKE2/K3s, Fleet GitOps, the AI Factory operator/UI, AI Library, and immutable blueprints provide the SUSE lifecycle layer.

- "Function library" is represented by NeMo Agent Toolkit functions and function groups.
- Qdrant and Milvus are example vector databases documented in SUSE AI Factory building blocks; OpenSearch is shown for hybrid search.
- SUSE Security and SUSE Observability are cross-cutting controls.

text:
Operating model:
- Signals originate in SUSE Observability, SUSE Security, and ITSM.
- Retrieval grounds the agent in topology, telemetry, CVEs, system state, and enterprise knowledge stored in vector/search services.
- Hermes and NeMo Agent Toolkit functions run inside the OpenShell policy sandbox.
- SUSE AI Universal Proxy, NeMo Switchyard, Guardrails, and NIM provide MCP governance, model routing, safety, and inference.
- The production path uses the SUSE Multi-Linux Manager / Uyuni MCP server for fleet changes.
- The direct SLES 16 MCP host path is optional, narrowly scoped, and technology preview.
- Writes require explicit approval and verification; write-capable Uyuni MCP tools can remain disabled until enabled by policy.

text:
Implementation guidance:
- Keep the Rancher Prime / AI Factory management cluster separate from AI Library workloads and the SUSE Observability cluster for production.
- Install SUSE Security controllers/managers/scanners centrally and an Enforcer on each protected Kubernetes node.
- Run OpenShell as gateway plus sandbox supervisor; Hermes is the restricted agent child.
- NeMo Agent Toolkit function groups expose typed internal tools and MCP clients.
- Route Nemotron 3.5 Lightning through a NIMService managed by NIM Operator. Serve Qwen 3.8 through a validated vLLM or SUSE Inference Endpoint unless a supported NIM profile is available.
- NIMCache and NIMService custom resources separate model staging from service lifecycle.
- Keep vector/search/object stores on encrypted persistent storage with tested backup/restore.
- Export application, model, MCP, Kubernetes, and host telemetry through local OTel collectors to SUSE Observability.
- Keep Uyuni MCP write tools disabled by default; require OAuth/mTLS and least-privilege roles before enabling bounded write actions.

text:
Implementation sequence:
- Phase 0 freezes architecture inputs and ownership.
- Phase 1 establishes recoverable cluster foundations.
- Phase 2 installs security and observability before application workloads.
- Phase 3 validates GPU and NIM lifecycle.
- Phase 4 establishes persistent data services and recovery.
- Phase 5 validates model endpoints and routing.
- Phase 6 proves agent policy containment and tool controls.
- Phase 7 integrates Multi-Linux Manager first as read-only, then enables bounded writes only after canary verification and rollback.
